### Approved to God
Author: Oswald Chambers
Site: My Utmost for His Highest
URL: https://utmost.org/updated/approved-to-god/
Passage: 2 Timothy 2:15
Points:
- Diligently study and wrestle with God's truth until you can explain your beliefs clearly.
- Merely borrowing words from others leaves truth without personal depth or power to help anyone else.
- Enduring the struggle of understanding transforms divine truth into strength for others.
- A conviction only becomes genuinely yours when forged through thoughtful reflection, study, and suffering.

### Don’t Use the “Hunt and Peck” Method...
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-april-8-2019.html
Passage: 2 Timothy 2:15
Points:
- Scripture should be read sequentially in complete context rather than by randomly opening to isolated verses.
- Quality of engagement and life application matter far more than the total quantity of pages read.
- Spending extended time truly absorbing a single verse is more fruitful than skimming large portions.
- Bible readers must ask what God is saying directly to them and put that truth into practice.

### Why You Must Study the Word for Yourself
Author: Courtnaye Richard
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/why-you-must-study-the-word-for-yourself-bible-study-minute-october-20-2017.html
Passage: 2 Timothy 2:15
Points:
- Believers must investigate Scripture for themselves to avoid being deceived by false teaching or human philosophy.
- The Holy Spirit equips faithful readers with spiritual discernment to distinguish truth from error.
- Like the Bereans, Christians should verify what they hear by comparing it directly to God's written word.
- Relying entirely on others for biblical knowledge leaves believers vulnerable to spiritual harm and falling away.

### The Lord's Honorable Vessels
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/lords-honorable-vessels
Passage: 2 Timothy 2:20-21
Points:
- Remaining faithful to the gospel sometimes requires painful separation from those who depart from sound doctrine.
- Paul illustrates spiritual fitness using household utensils, contrasting noble instruments with common disposal pots.
- Believers become ready and useful for the Master's work by turning away from moral impurity and false doctrine.
- Although God graciously grants honor to redeemed sinners, believers are called to actively pursue personal holiness.
